patch_description: Replace the placeholder with a deterministic hybrid optimizer for the 13-point Heilbronn triangle problem. The approach combines: (1) multi-start initialization using both 3-fold rotationally symmetric configurations (center + jittered concentric rings, exploiting the known tendency of optimal Heilbronn configurations toward 3-fold symmetry) and seeded uniform random starts; (2) a targeted local search that repeatedly identifies the globally smallest triangle and moves its three vertices along the gradient of that triangle's signed area (with line-search step adaptation and re-targeting among the worst triangles when stalled, which escapes local optima of the non-smooth min objective); and (3) a smooth softmin (LogSumExp-weighted) polish pass whose gradients flow toward all near-minimal triangles simultaneously. Points are confined to the unit square (a convex region of unit area), and the objective is the scale-invariant ratio (smallest triangle area) / (convex hull area), computed with a monotone-chain hull. Only improving moves (in the true minimum triangle area) are accepted, guaranteeing monotone progress; fixed seeds and fixed iteration counts guarantee deterministic, reproducible output across runs and platforms.
